lines.text: Your agent stops and asks permission to run a command, and waits for you to say yes.
You see the request and you tap Allow, within seconds of the question appearing.
Then nothing happens. The agent sits there, as if you had never answered.
A full minute passes before it finally notices, and you wonder if something has crashed.
The reason is that the agent only checks for replies on a timer, and the timer had not fired yet.
Agents that check for replies on a timer always have a delay. The longer the timer, the longer you wait.
A shorter timer wastes work asking over and over, so you get lag or noise, never neither.
Agent R Q pushes your reply to Claude Code over a live stream, the moment you send it.
It arrives through Claude Code's own notification channel, so the agent does not poll at all.
The moment you answer, the agent moves. The migration starts in the same second.
You stop wondering if it crashed, because every answer gets a response straight away.
How long does your agent usually wait on you? Tell us your record below, and try live notifications at Agent R Q dot com.
